claims.text: Nickel-based superalloy components will significantly reduce corrosion compared with conventional steel components in hot-dip aluminum plating equipment.
Nickel-based superalloy components will extend service life compared with conventional steel components in hot-dip aluminum plating equipment.
The initial components are conventional steel components exposed to high-temperature liquid aluminum.
Conventional steel components are to be replaced with nickel-based superalloy components.
The relevant components are subjected to high-temperature liquid aluminum during hot-dip aluminum plating.
Nickel-based superalloys possess corrosion resistance under the stated conditions.
Nickel-based superalloys possess thermal stability under the stated conditions.
Nickel-based superalloys have greater elevated-temperature oxidation resistance than conventional steels.
Nickel-based superalloys have greater elevated-temperature corrosion resistance than conventional steels.
The elevated-temperature oxidation and corrosion resistance of nickel-based superalloys protects components from erosion by liquid aluminum.
Nickel-based superalloy components will exhibit less wear than conventional steel components.
Nickel-based superalloy components will exhibit less corrosion than conventional steel components.
Nickel-based superalloy components will have at least 50% longer service life than conventional steel components.
Conventional steel components have a service life of approximately one year under similar conditions.
The proposed effect is limited to components in direct contact with high-temperature liquid aluminum during hot-dip plating.
The percentage of service-life extension may vary with alloy composition and operating conditions.
